inspiration: Latch-and-drain creature: the parasite has drain, break-free and death frame groups (game/m_parasite.c lines 366, 390, 459). A creature that attaches makes the threat a state as well as damage. Keep the latched state; change the silhouette and the drain cue.

Hover-to-land creature: takeoff, land, forward and backward chains, three pain variants and a death chain (game/m_hover.c lines 127, 226, 232, 352). An airborne enemy that lands for close attacks is readable. Keep the takeoff-land switch; change the hull.

Defensive stance telegraph: the brain has a defense group and a duck group before its attacks (game/m_brain.c lines 244, 339). A visible guard pose is a telegraph the player can read. Keep the telegraph; change the posture.

Gib threshold per creature: a hit below the gib value plays a gib death with bone, meat and a head; a normal hit plays the ordinary death (game/m_parasite.c lines 475-478; game/m_brain.c lines 586-590). Keep the threshold as zone or creature data; change the gib pieces to armour plates and sparks.
Death clears status: brain_die clears its effects flag and power-armour type first (game/m_brain.c lines 586-591). A death resets active buffs so a corpse does not keep a glow.
Data-first item table: one row per item with a classname and a reserved index 0 (game/g_items.c lines 1134-1147, 1499).
Fixed-width scoreboard columns keep numbers aligned in a text table (ctf/layout.txt line 3). Keep the column idea; change to icon columns at 375 wide.

briefs.label: Latch-and-drain leech (creature)
briefs.why: A creature that latches on turns the fight into a state the player must break, not only a damage number.
briefs.keep: a latch or drain frame group; a break-free group; a death chain; the latched state is visible on the player
briefs.change: a crab-like shell silhouette instead of a worm; a bruised violet colour; drain shown as a rim glow on the player, not a sprite on the creature

briefs.label: Hover craft that lands (creature)
briefs.why: An airborne enemy that drops to land for close attacks is readable at phone width because the height change is the signal.
briefs.keep: takeoff and land chains; forward and backward movement; a short death chain
briefs.change: a different hull and thruster glow; a ground-shadow cue before landing; no craft-shaped body

briefs.label: Guard stance telegraph (creature)
briefs.why: A visible guard pose before attacks gives the player a window to react, which is the readability goal at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: a defense group and a duck group before the attack; three pain variants
briefs.change: our own posture and a shield flash instead of a brain-shaped head; a different guard colour

briefs.label: Gib-threshold death (death presentation)
briefs.why: Big hits get a different death, so the player feels the damage size; the threshold is per creature.
briefs.keep: a per-creature gib threshold; a gib burst on big hits; the normal death otherwise
briefs.change: armour plates and sparks instead of bone and meat; the threshold stored as zone or creature data
